title: Municipal infrastructure resilience depends less on project need than on local fiscal, workforce, and grant-management capacity
source_unit: National League of Cities, Municipal Infrastructure Conditions Report 2026 and Municipal Infrastructure Conditions Survey
geography: United States; responding cities, towns, and villages, with comparison to 2022 municipal infrastructure survey results

observations.period: 2026; municipal infrastructure condition and priority assessment

denominator.unit: responding municipalities represented in the infrastructure-condition assessment

categories.unit: infrastructure categories graded by municipal respondents

condition_pattern.value: Some asset types stabilized or improved slightly while others remained under increasing strain amid aging assets and rising construction costs

top_priorities.value: Streets, water, sewer, stormwater, and water-treatment systems remained core capital priorities; public buildings, parking, broadband, and public transit were lower priorities for many respondents

mechanism.value: Local quality of life and safety depend on infrastructure systems whose condition and priority are filtered through municipal capacity and competing daily services

observations.method: National League of Cities survey of municipal leaders assessing infrastructure conditions and priorities, with comparison to 2022 results.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is a responding-municipality sample, not a national engineering condition inventory; ratings are self-assessments and category priorities may reflect local mandates and budgets.
observations.subgroup: Cities, towns, and villages with different sizes, fiscal bases, infrastructure portfolios, and access to federal programs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower priority for broadband or transit may reflect existing capacity, different local responsibility, or survey framing rather than lower resident need; condition improvement may be uneven within a municipality.

observations.period: 2026; municipal infrastructure finance and local fiscal room

denominator.unit: municipal finance framework summarized by the NLC report; property-tax reliance and revenue figures are reported aggregate patterns

property_tax_share.unit: percent of municipal tax revenue represented by property taxes in the report's summary

city_reliance.unit: percent of cities relying on property taxes as a municipal revenue foundation according to the report summary

cash_based_shift.value: Compared with 2022, surveyed municipalities increasingly relied on locally generated, cash-based funding and reserves rather than borrowing

mechanism.value: Fiscal caution can protect debt capacity while reducing the speed or scale of long-lived infrastructure renewal

observations.method: NLC synthesis of survey responses and municipal infrastructure-finance patterns; property-tax figures are reported in the public summary rather than estimated here as a causal funding model.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not provide a complete municipal balance-sheet distribution or establish that cash-based funding caused project delays or improved fiscal resilience.
observations.subgroup: Municipalities with different property-tax bases, reserves, borrowing capacity, service burdens, and revenue structures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cash-based funding may reflect prudent fiscal management or available federal and local resources; borrowing can also accelerate necessary projects when repayment capacity is sound.

denominator.unit: municipal respondents represented in the capital-decision factor comparison

funding_availability.value: Funding availability was the single most important reported influence on capital investment decisions

staff_capacity.value: Staff capacity was among the factors emphasized by respondents in determining which projects move forward and how quickly

strategic_plans.value: Strategic plans and elected officials' priorities also shaped municipal capital decisions

year_comparison_boundary.value: Differences between 2022 and 2026 factor ratings were not statistically significant, potentially because of small samples

mechanism.value: Infrastructure need becomes realized investment only through money, administrative workforce, planning, and political prioritization

observations.method: NLC comparison of municipal survey responses about factors influencing capital decisions in 2022 and 2026.
observations.uncertainty: The survey identifies reported influences, not project-level causal weights, execution rates, or differences in resident outcomes; small samples constrain year comparisons.
observations.subgroup: Municipal leaders and staff responsible for capital planning and infrastructure investment.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may emphasize funding because it is salient while technical design, procurement, land, permitting, or community opposition constrain projects in ways not captured by the summary.

observations.period: 2021-2026; federal infrastructure grants and local implementation capacity

denominator.unit: cities identified by NLC Rebuilding Together analysis as having secured federal infrastructure funding

federal_funding_secured.unit: billion dollars in federal infrastructure funding secured by more than 1,600 cities in the NLC analysis

grant_value.value: Federal grants were particularly valuable for transportation and water infrastructure

local_capacity_condition.value: The report emphasizes that local capacity to pursue, manage, and implement grants determines how fully communities can leverage federal investment

mechanism.value: Federal money is an input, not a realized local outcome; administrative capacity mediates whether grants become functioning, maintained public systems

observations.method: NLC report synthesis of Rebuilding Together grant analysis and municipal survey evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The aggregate funding figure does not establish project completion, distributional incidence, service quality, maintenance, or household benefit; cities may differ greatly in capacity and project scale.
observations.subgroup: Cities receiving federal infrastructure funds, municipal grant-management teams, residents relying on transportation and water systems, and communities with different technical capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Grant acquisition may itself build administrative capacity, and federal investment can have benefits before full project completion through planning, employment, or system assessment.

related_sources.claim: Official full NLC Municipal Infrastructure Conditions Report 2026 PDF.
NLC Rebuilding Together infrastructure-funding analysis referenced in the report.

boundary: This record adds a U.S. local-capacity route from infrastructure condition and public need through municipal finance, staff capacity, elected priorities, federal grants, implementation, and public-system reliability. It is a municipal leader survey and advocacy-organization synthesis, not a national engineering inventory, causal evaluation, project-completion dataset, or proof of household outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official NLC report page and downloadable PDF were reviewed for survey sample notes, infrastructure categories, funding patterns, capital-decision factors, federal grant totals, and local-capacity boundaries.
